newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh allows private management in railway.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh allows private management in railway.

text.p: A Bangladesh private company on Monday took over the operation of a rail route as part of the country's drive to open its state-run railway to the private sector, railway officials said.
They said the involvement of the private sector was an experiment to improve efficiency and reduce the country's deficit.
"It's an experiment. If it clicks, we can lease out commercial management of other short distance routes," said one official.

H.A. International Ltd, the firm which won the two-year management contract of the 15-kilometre (9-mile) passenger rail route connecting the capital Dhaka with the industrial town of Narayanganj, pledged cleaner compartments and the maintenance of rail schedules.
The rail sector has been losing passengers to road transport because of poor management.
"We will try to bring back those passengers," said an official with H.A. International.
The Bangladesh government spends about one billion taka ($23 million) every year in railway subsidies.
